newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: SAVINGS BANK'S PROFIT SOARS IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: SAVINGS BANK'S PROFIT SOARS IN 1996.

text.p: Lithuania's huge state-run Savings Bank said on Tuesday that its 1996 net profit soared to 30 million litas compared with a loss of 39 million litas the previous year.
The bank, which is almost 75 percent state-owned, said in a statement that it would pay out dividends of 0.75 litas per one share litas.
The bank said that most of its revenue and profit came from loans, domestic T-bills, and services.
It added that its net profit for the first two months of this year was two million litas but gave no compaisions with the same period last year.
The bank's share capital last year rose from 20 million litas to 40 million litas and will soon be increased to 60 million litas, the bank said.
The Lithuanian government will decide at its weekly meeting on Wednesday if it will retain its stake of almost 75 percent in the new injection of share capital.
The bank also said that its deposits rose during the year to 1.0324 billion litas from 855.3 million litas.
The bank added that its assets rose in 1996 to 1.1802 billion litas from 937.8 million litas, an increase of 23.6 percent.

The bank, the second largest in Lithuania in terms of assets, has not been included on the government's privatisation agenda although it has not ruled out the possibility of eventually selling the bank off.
The government has firmly committed itself to the privatisation of the country's other state-run banks, the Agricultural Bank and the troubled State Commercial Bank.
